title: Infinite armor set generator, leverages an ubermesh and a uv atlas key.
author: Dirly

comments.author: Dirly
comments.body: workflow: I set up a pretty complex UV system with an ubermesh.  basically all the geometry for all pieces of equipment are on 1 single model.  I create a key dictating what each piece is and what it should be possibly made of. The key is color coded and sent with the prompt to a diffusion model.   That model is given the key, given what each peice of the key is on the model, and then the style/look it is goign for.  There are still some hiccups, specially with shading of hood rims, and other parts, but I believe its very passable.  The beauty of this system is that you can also do it for mobs as well, basically reskinning any model at will to fit the story you are going for.  My hope is to make an mmo where every armor, and every server actually feels and looks unique.

replies.author: Dirly
replies.body: The meshes are made in blockbench by me by hand.  I then unwrapped each uv a specific way so it would fit into the uv a specific way so it would still kinda retain the shape of the object to some degree. I then color code each UV with a key.  I wrote the prompt that told the ai what each peice was supposed to look like...  it still requires some human work to pull it off well.

replies.author: Dirly
replies.body:
basically I made a low poly model, broke it down into various parts, arm, legs, helm, shoulders, robes ect.  Each one I tried to unwrap to still make it be able to be seen by an image gen as what it was.  So arm was still looking like an arm from the side view ect.  I then color code all the UVs and created a pretty comprehensive prompt on what each piece is, what it could possibly have on it ( like plumage on helms ect).  The prompt is pretty extensive and only works for each model you create, but after you lay that out, you then can add to the prompt what style or look you are going for.  

Those styles are basically generated from my world generator, which creates a world, the story behind it and then determines what the armor/equipment would look like for that area.

replies.author: Dirly
replies.body: One note ubermeshes, like this will not perform well with crazy hi tris, you will hit performance bottlenecking. Tripo from what I've toyed around with is not too great with that, and struggles with very small poly counts.   I made that model with 500 tris in mind.

comments.author: phoenixArc27
comments.body: How does this handle 3d geometry that hangs off the body like shoulders and cloth skirts? And what about weights?

replies.author: Dirly
replies.body: I mean thats just a plane (well flat geometry), the prompt requests that the textures are created on a pure white background.  all the white is cut away.  so if they want lets say a frayed robe at the bottom and it is textured white, the code cuts that away.  much easier with low res textures tho.  The sholders are just hard connected to the bone at the top,  the robes are painted with weights I need to fix it a bit as the run cycle the legs crash through the back but for the most part it looks good.
